title: Bought under fake names
body: In 1964 and 1965 Walt Disney's company quietly bought about 27,000 acres of central Florida swamp and cattle land through dummy corporations with names like the Latin-American Development and Management Corporation and the Reedy Creek Ranch Corporation. One of them, M.T. Lott, is a pun on "empty lot". The secrecy kept prices from spiking, and the land averaged about $180 an acre. An Orlando newspaper reporter worked out who the buyer was in October 1965, weeks before the company announced the project.
